question: Can thermodynamic observables partition the full set of nontrivial two-dimensional binary totalistic cellular-automaton rules into interpretable behavioral classes?

key_findings.claim: The paper maps live cells to independent unit energy states and defines entropy, temperature, heat capacity, Helmholtz free energy, pressure, and an activity temperature through benchmark, finite partition-function, and ideal-gas analogies.
key_findings.evidence: The construction explicitly does not assume Hamiltonian evolution or energy conservation; the resulting quantities are diagnostic analogies rather than literal thermodynamic state variables.

key_findings.claim: Rules are classified as dead or into four ideal/non-ideal and equilibrium/non-equilibrium combinations using coefficients of variation and spatial partitions.
key_findings.evidence: Dead rules become inactive by 100 iterations; equilibrium compares local Helmholtz free-energy variation, while ideal-gas behavior compares ideal and activity temperatures over the first 25 steps using selected thresholds.

key_findings.claim: The energy-density uniformity check supports one modeling assumption for most rules, but the work does not establish that its new classes predict canonical Wolfram complexity or computational universality.
key_findings.evidence: For 17,684 of 18,150 rules the partition energy-density spread is below 0.1; the conclusion proposes connections to conventional complexity classification and non-equilibrium behavior as future work.

method.core_idea: Treat occupancy and activity statistics of cellular automata as thermodynamic analogues and classify every nontrivial outer-totalistic rule with these aggregate observables.
method.mechanism: Run rules from random initial states on finite grids, compute three families of energy/entropy/temperature/free-energy quantities, partition grids to test spatial uniformity, and threshold temporal coefficients of variation into dead, equilibrium, and ideal-gas-like categories.
assumptions: Cell occupancies can be modeled as independent unit energy contributions.
Finite-grid spatial boxes are large enough to approximate local thermodynamic behavior.
Chosen time windows, random initial conditions, and empirical thresholds are representative of a rule's behavior.

techniques.role: Maps occupancy trajectories to entropy, temperatures, free energy, heat capacity, and pressure.
Measures spatial dispersion across 25 grid boxes.
Evaluates 18,150 nontrivial reduced-Moore rules under boundary and size variants.

evaluations.setting: All 18,150 nontrivial binary totalistic reduced-Moore-neighborhood rules on 100x100 and 400x400 grids with closed or periodic boundaries.
evaluations.metric: Inactivity, coefficient of variation of free energy and temperature ratios, and spatial energy-density spread over 100 steps.
evaluations.result: The scheme populates five behavioral classes and is broadly stable to size/boundary changes; most rules satisfy the selected energy-uniformity check.
evaluations.baseline: Comparisons among benchmark, partition-function, and ideal-gas thermodynamic analogies, not against established CA complexity labels.

limitations: Temperature, pressure, and free energy depend on ad hoc occupancy-energy analogies in a non-Hamiltonian deterministic system.
Class thresholds and observation horizons are empirically chosen and sensitivity is not fully quantified.
The sweep uses one neighborhood/rule family and largely random initial conditions.
No direct predictive test against computation, phase-transition, or Wolfram/Li-Packard behavior labels is provided.
failure_modes: Long transients or rare initial conditions cause a rule to be mislabeled after 100 steps.
Boundary and finite-size effects move a rule across an empirical threshold.
Aggregate occupancy statistics collapse spatial patterns with very different computational complexity.
reusable_insights: Exhaustive rule-space studies should report sensitivity to initial conditions, size, boundaries, thresholds, and horizon.
Physical analogies become more useful when tied to an independently measured behavioral outcome.
Local spatial dispersion can reveal structure hidden by global density averages.
open_questions: Do these thermodynamic classes predict Wolfram class, phase transitions, or computational universality on held-out rules?
How stable are assignments under ensembles of initial states and much longer horizons?
Can interaction-aware energies or transfer entropy capture structure missed by independent occupancy?

competitive_landscape.title: Cell-centric heuristics for the classification of cellular automata
competitive_landscape.difference: Barbosa et al. use input and transition entropies to discriminate Wolfram classes; the target introduces equilibrium and ideal-gas analogues for a large 2D totalistic rule space.

competitive_landscape.title: Phase Transitions of Cellular Automata
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct statistical-mechanics treatment of CA phase behavior.
competitive_landscape.difference: Bagnoli and Rechtman analyze phase transitions with mean-field and renormalization tools; the target constructs an empirical thermodynamic taxonomy rather than estimating critical behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Automated Cellular Automaton Classification
competitive_landscape.difference: Rollier et al. train a CNN to recognize mesoscopic Li-Packard classes from spacetime diagrams; the target uses hand-designed thermodynamic aggregates and produces different labels.

novelty_assessment: The exhaustive 2D rule sweep and thermodynamic five-way taxonomy are novel and visually useful. The mapping is heuristic, and its scientific value depends on future demonstrations that the labels predict independent dynamical or computational properties.
reviewer_notes: Read all 24 extracted pages, including derivations and rule enumeration. The review avoids treating the constructed thermodynamic variables as literal equilibrium quantities. Primary competitor sources checked 2026-08-23.
